title: ELEC EMER CONFIG

alert.trigger: AC BUS 1 and AC BUS 2 are not supplied.

effectivity.note: Procedure lines identical; STATUS INOP SYS and centre-tank fuel differ.

summary: Both AC main buses are lost. The RAT drives the emergency generator, leaving essentially CM1 instruments, VHF1/HF1/ATC1 and alternate law (direct law with gear down). CM1 flies manually as PF while the PM works the ECAM; after STATUS the crew uses the QRH summary to decide, prepare and fly the approach at no less than 140 kt.

background.text: RAT extends automatically when AC BUS 1 and 2 are lost above 100 kt; blue hydraulics drive the EMER GEN, which supplies AC ESS and (via ESS TR) DC ESS.
If the RAT stalls, the network transfers to the batteries and static inverter, and AC/DC SHED ESS are shed. On ground: DC BAT BUS connected below 100 kt; AC ESS shed below 50 kt (all displays lost).
EMER ELEC PWR MAN ON (guarded): manual RAT extension; EMER GEN couples 3 s after the RAT supplies it. Red FAULT light: EMER GEN not supplying power.
Remaining: FLY — PFD1, alternate law; NAVIGATE — ND1, FMGC1, RMP1, VOR1/ILS1, DME1; COMMUNICATE — VHF1, HF1, ATC1. On batteries FAC1 and FMGC1 are also lost.
Secondary failures are inhibited on the ECAM in ELEC EMER CONFIG.

technique.text: Red LAND ASAP, but approaching a poorly equipped airfield in marginal weather is unwise; prolonged flight is not recommended.
A clear reading of STATUS is essential to sequence actions during the approach.
Complex procedure: use the QRH summary after the ECAM procedure.
BSCUs lost: no NWS or anti-skid; alternate braking with yellow hydraulics up to 1 000 PSI; no reversers.
RA 1+2 lost with their automatic callouts — the PM makes the callouts.
Approaching 50 kt on the landing roll, all display units are lost.
